# dsh-decisions-classifiers
OpenAI **Decisions API** classifiers for DeepSeek Harness.

The Decisions API (`POST /v1/decisions`, model `gpt-6-luna`) answers typed questions about text
and

images instead of generating prose: a **predicate** returns the probability that a condition
holds,

a **choice** returns one of your options with the full probability distribution, and a
**score** ret

urns a probability-weighted average over ordered levels. This plugin puts that
capability in four pl

a probability-weighted average over ordered levels. This plugin puts that
capability in four places.
| Surface | What it gives you |
| Agent tools | `decisions_classify` (one built-in classifier), `decisions_ask` (arbitrary typed que

stions, up to ~10 per request), `decisions_status` |
| Cordis service | `decisionsClassifiers` — `li

stPresets()`, `classify()`, `ask()`, `status()` for other plugins |
| Opt-in call gate | Classify ev

ery `run_code`/`bash`/`write`/`edit` call before it executes and deny the flagged ones |
| Advice ca
rd | A "classifier opinion" card beside `ask_user_question` multiple-choice prompts, with one click
assifier opinion" card beside `ask_user_question` multiple-choice prompts, with one click to adopt |

Anything else goes through `decisions_ask`, which takes the wire question types directly.
## Setup

1. Install the bundle (see below).
2. Open **Settings → Decisions Classifiers**, paste an OpenAI API

key, and press **Store key**.
The key is written through the DSH credential seam as `OPENAI_API_KEY

` (or the env name you
set) and is never read back by the page. `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the process envi

ronment or a
`.env` file works too.
3. Press **Test connection**.

## What the numbers mean

The endpoint returns a probability distribution over a support, then projects it: `choice` takes
the

argmax, `score` takes the expectation of the zero-based level index, and `predicate` has
nothing to

project. Those projections are where the interpretation lives, and they are not
equally portable.
| type | support comes from | scalar you get | portable? |

| `predicate` | the world (true/false) | `probability` | **yes** — the one number that travels |
| `

choice` | **your options list** | `choice` (argmax) | no — menu-dependent |
| `score` | **your order
ed levels** | `score` = E[index] | no — level-dependent, and metric-imposing |

**`predicate` is the only portable scalar.** It is a Bernoulli parameter, so it is calibratable
agai

nst realized outcomes (reliability diagrams, Brier score) and thresholdable against a cost
rule. One

caveat matters more than it looks: the endpoint accepts *any* input, so many predicates
are subject

ive ("is this code maintainable?"). There, `probability` is not a property of the
world — it is a ma

rginal over a rule set nobody wrote. Calibration still works, but its referent
becomes *your* raters

instead of reality: it licenses "consistent with our standard", never
"true".

**`choice` distributions are menu-dependent.** The support is your options list, so relabeling
the m

enu moves the numbers while the world stays put. Measured on one fixed top category, with
only the t
ail split ever more finely:
| menu | max p | sum p² | top-2 gap |

Two candidate concentration measures move in **opposite directions** under that relabeling. So a
4-o

ption and a 2-option question in the same batch are not comparable on any confidence number,
and the
interpretable signal is the **top-2 margin** — how close the routing is to a coin flip.

**`score` is an ordinal position presented as an interval.** Levels carry only `label` and
`descript

ion`; the API assigns indices 0..n-1 by position, with no client-supplied weight or
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations

- **Images must be inline base64.** The endpoint rejects hosted HTTP(S) URLs and `file_id`
inputs, s

o `decisions_ask` reads local paths and inlines them. DSH attachments cannot be passed
through by re

ference.
- **One model.** `gpt-6-luna` is the only available model while the API is in public beta.

- **The advice card sends the questions only**, not the surrounding conversation transcript;
decisio

ns that depend on earlier chat turns may be less well informed.
- **The gate fails open** on a netwo

rk or credential error, and logs the failure: a classification
outage must not block every tool call

.
- **`confidence` is surfaced but should not be thresholded.** It is undocumented and
menu-dependen

t; see What the numbers mean.
- **`score` assumes equally spaced levels**, which the API imposes and

you cannot override.
- Pricing is input-token only ($0.10 per 1M tokens for `gpt-6-luna`), but this

plugin does not
meter spend.
